comments.body:
ROOT-CAUSE INVESTIGATION (rebar-debug) — db1c was PARTLY, not fully, fixed by d59e.

Verified against origin/main @ 8ffdcea0d.

## What d59e (99e22e4c2) already fixed

- AC1 (a ticket whose description alone nears the budget still produces a verdict): DONE. `_MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS` is now 100,000 (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py`), and `tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_recovery_oversized_d59e.py::test_a_real_blocked_ticket_now_reaches_a_verdict` is parametrized on ticket 2932's EXACT reported size (41,595 chars).
- AC2 (recovery budget documented alongside the main pass, relationship stated): DONE at `docs/llm-framework.md:524-531`, including the criteria <= context invariant.

## What was still live

- AC3 (the error message must not recommend shortening the description without noting it invalidates the plan-review attestation): STILL LIVE. Confirmed at runtime — `recovery_failure_cause()` in `src/rebar/llm/failure.py:414-418` still emitted: 'so the recovery pass was refused before it ran — shorten the ticket's description/comments.'

Proven root cause: BOTH halves of that remedy are unactionable, for two different reasons, each contradicted by code already on main.

1. description — `material_fingerprint()` at `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py:715-732` hashes the description into the plan-review attestation ('a material edit invalidates the signature'). Editing it to clear the completion gate trips `require_plan_review_for_close`. The remedy for one close gate is a guaranteed failure of the other.
2. comments — comments are explicitly NON-material (attestation-safe to edit), but the store is append-only: `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:511` exposes `comment()` with NO delete or redact counterpart. That lever does not exist at all.

Corroborating: d59e itself shipped a test whose docstring says the remedy 'could not be carried out', while leaving the message printing it unchanged.

## On the reported NON-DETERMINISM — explained, not a separate defect

Recovery is entered only when the PRIMARY pass raises a token-exhaustion `UnretryableOutputError` (`completion_recovery.py` `CompletionAgentStep.run` -> `_is_token_exhaustion`). Whether the primary exhausts is model-dependent, so the same ticket can take the recovery path on one attempt and not the next — exactly the attempt-2-fails / attempt-3-passes pattern reported. That is the fallback design, not a bug. With the cap at 100,000, entering recovery no longer means a refusal for any real ticket, so the flaky-refusal symptom is gone at its source.

## Fix pushed

Gerrit change 1116 — https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1116
Confined to `src/rebar/llm/failure.py` (message + docstring) plus a new test `tests/unit/test_close_gate_bound_remedy_db1c.py`. No bound, exception type, diagnostic key or control flow changed.

New operator message:
'The ticket's context (100,001 chars) exceeds the bounded completion-recovery limit (100,000 chars), so the recovery pass was refused before it ran. The context cannot simply be made smaller: its comments are append-only (the store has no redaction operation), and its description is material, so editing it invalidates the plan-review attestation, which would then have to be re-earned. Its gate_error_v1 sidecar holds the full diagnostic.'

## Evidence for AC4 (three consecutive attempts, identical content)

Driving `CompletionAgentStep` with a 41,595-char context (ticket 2932's size) three times with byte-identical content: verdicts ['PASS', 'PASS', 'PASS']. Under the pre-d59e 24,000 cap this size was refused before the pass ran.

Test discipline: the new test was confirmed RED on both bug assertions before any fix existed, held out from the implementing subagent, and returned to RED under a mutation restoring the old literal. Full unit suite after: 6274 passed, 20 skipped. lint + typecheck clean.

Sibling sweep for the bug class ('operator remedy names an unreachable lever'): no other instance in `src/` outside the reconciler surface.

compiled_state.description:
# Completion-recovery context bound conflicts with the verifier's own remediation advice

## Context / Problem

Closing story 2932 hit:

```
cannot close 2932-8a98-6d70-4550: completion verification could not run
(step 'decide@then/verify' failed: completion recovery context bound exceeded).
The ticket's context (41,595 chars) exceeds the bounded completion-recovery limit (24,000 chars),
so the recovery pass was refused before it ran — shorten the ticket's description/comments.
```

MEASURED composition of that ticket at the time: description **21,728** chars, 8 comments totalling **19,410** chars (41,138 total).

Two things make this more than a one-off size complaint:

1. **The description ALONE was 21,728 of the 24,000 budget.** Even with every comment deleted, that ticket has ~2.3k chars of headroom for its entire evidence history. For a plan of this size the recovery pass is effectively unreachable, permanently.

2. **The bound fights the verifier's own remediation instruction.** When a criterion is unmet the verifier says: *'add a comment to this ticket that documents the evidence — cite the concrete artifacts...'*. Following that advice is what pushed 2932 over the limit: a first close attempt failed on ONE unmet [operator-attested] criterion (correctly — its evidence named a Verified +1 from a superseded patchset), and the ~3.5k-char comment recording the current evidence is what tipped it past the bound. So the gate asked for evidence and then refused to run because the evidence was added.

## Reproduction / observed behaviour

- attempt 1: main verification RAN and returned a substantive per-criterion verdict (1 unmet).
- attempt 2 (after adding the evidence comment): refused at `decide@then/verify` on the recovery bound.
- `rebar compact <id>` does NOT help — it snapshots the event log, leaving description+comment TEXT unchanged (verified: 41,138 before and after).
- attempt 3: SUCCEEDED and the ticket closed, with no content change between attempts 2 and 3.

That last point matters: the failure is **NOT deterministic** on ticket size. It fires only when the recovery path is entered (the main pass has a different, larger budget). So the same ticket can fail and then pass with identical content, which makes it read as a flake while actually being a real bound.

## Why the workarounds are bad

- **Shorten the description** — the description IS the plan-review-attested material. Editing it changes the material fingerprint and invalidates the attestation, which `require_plan_review_for_close` then demands be re-earned. So the remedy for a close-gate problem is to break the other close-gate precondition.
- **`--force-close`** — discards the completion gate entirely for exactly the large, complex tickets where it is most valuable, and AGENTS.md rightly frames force as an operator judgment call rather than a routine move.
- **Retry until it passes** — what actually worked here, but it is cargo-culting a nondeterministic bound.

## Candidate directions (not a decision)

- Give the recovery pass the same budget as the main verification pass, or derive it from the model's real context window rather than a fixed 24,000.
- Budget the recovery input by TRUNCATING/summarizing oldest comments rather than refusing the whole pass — a bounded pass over recent evidence beats no pass.
- Prioritise the evidence the verifier itself asked for (most recent comments) over the oldest history when packing that budget.
- At minimum: make the error distinguish 'this ticket can never fit' (description alone exceeds budget) from 'this attempt did not fit', and stop advising a fix ("shorten the description") that invalidates the plan attestation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a test constructs a ticket whose description alone approaches the recovery budget and asserts the completion gate still produces a verdict (pass or fail) rather than refusing to run
- [ ] the recovery pass's budget is documented alongside the main verification pass's, with the relationship between them stated
- [ ] the error message no longer recommends shortening the description without noting that doing so invalidates the plan-review attestation
- [ ] [operator-attested] a FIXTURE ticket sized like 2932 (~21.7k description, ~19.4k comments) produces a
      completion verdict on 3 consecutive attempts, evidenced by the three run outputs in a comment.
      NOTE: worded against a fixture because ticket 2932 is already CLOSED and cannot be closed again —
      the original wording named an artifact that can no longer exist.
compiled_state.title: Completion-recovery context bound is unreachable for tickets whose plan alone nears the limit
